**Swarms — generation** — drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return
candid
ates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempot
ency-Key` — a call\nwith no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and offering one would imply the\ndrafts are stable across retries

when they are not.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goa
ls for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed *

*by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the
model cost is on\n> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst b
rake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own
daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `R
etry-After` — honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so

do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms — runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/run

s`,
`.../goal-runs/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../g
oals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |\n| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out
has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sp
onsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report
`funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-se
ssion `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n|
`POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409`

|

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model c
redits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped
: true` and starts no second runner —\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined\n to ident
ify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status:
\"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: th
e runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments c

an
 resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>\
n> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minu
te burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally carry `Retry-Afte

r`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll

-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

|
Endpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat fa
ilures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET ...
/goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a
finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a
swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — s

cheduled, not done |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic tr

aps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the

session total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failed
GradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a\n regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the o

ther.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —
`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *
not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismissed, and hiding one ne

ver claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is o
n\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and use
r-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting; `force: true` deli

berately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (wait seco
nds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403

` means
> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId
}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did,
and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it ex

ists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republ
ishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/s
tudy` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../stud
ies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per
session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcrip
t, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visi
tors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No bo
dy — the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `
invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending
their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |\n

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from granting NEW ac
cess; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n
> is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did n

ot intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, tigh
tening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> st

ops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Re

ad `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.
